[PATH:empirical] OECD Regional Well-Being and Environmental Accounting Databases (2010-2023) — These datasets provide quantitative measures of community success (e.g., subjective well-being, income, employment) alongside regional ecological footprint and carrying capacity estimates, enabling direct testing of whether normalization against carrying capacity improves correlation with GDP-adjusted indicators.

[PATH:literature] The Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI) and Index of Sustainable Economic Welfare (ISEW) literature — These frameworks already attempt to integrate social and environmental factors into economic measurement. Reviewing studies that apply GPI/ISEW to OECD regions since 2010 can reveal whether normalization against ecological carrying capacity is necessary for consistent integration of community narratives with GDP.

[PATH:empirical] Case-control studies comparing OECD communities with high vs. low ecological carrying capacity normalization (e.g., Scandinavian vs. Mediterranean regions) — Empirical comparison of community success metrics (e.g., life satisfaction, social capital indices) before and after normalization against regional carrying capacity can isolate the effect of normalization on the narrative-GDP relationship, confirming or refuting the hypothesis.

evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Community-based success narratives because subjective well-being indices inherently conflict with economic output metrics]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative longitudinal studies of subjective well-being (SWB) indices and GDP per capita in post-2000 community-based development projects (e.g., Bhutan's Gross National Happiness index vs. GDP growth) — Directly tests the hypothesized inherent conflict by examining whether communities with high SWB scores systematically exhibit lower GDP growth, or vice versa, across diverse global contexts.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of literature on the Easterlin Paradox and related critiques of GDP as a welfare metric (e.g., Kahneman & Deaton, 2010; Stiglitz-Sen-Fitoussi Commission report) — Provides theoretical and empirical grounding for the claimed conflict, synthesizing existing evidence on the divergence between economic output and subjective well-being at community scales.

[PATH:theoretical] Agent-based modeling simulations of community economies incorporating both production metrics and SWB indicators to assess trade-offs under varying policy regimes — Allows controlled exploration of causal mechanisms behind the hypothesized conflict, testing whether SWB and GDP are inherently antagonistic or can be aligned under certain conditions.
